item.title: NBC Western revives local broadcasting from temporary studio in Daru
item.description: After nearly five years of silence, National Broadcasting Corporation in Western has returned to the airwaves with the launch of a temporary studio in Daru today. NBC Western has revived local broadcasting in the province, backed by a five-man engineering team restoring relay stations across the province.
item.content:encoded:
After nearly five years of silence, National Broadcasting Corporation in Western has returned to the airwaves with the launch of a temporary studio in Daru today.

NBC Western has revived local broadcasting in the province, backed by a five-man engineering team restoring relay stations across the province.

Long-time broadcaster and outgoing director provincial radio Sam Sabiyam went on air this afternoon during a trial transmission, marking the official return of NBC Western to the airwaves after nearly five years off air.

The revival also marked the decommissioning of the station’s old Air 4 analogue console. NBC Western’s two studio technicians arrived in Daru yesterday from Port Moresby and will now set up the new DMX 8 digital console in the permanent studio.

A five-man NBC engineering team is currently on the ground working to restore four relay stations in Daru, Tapila, Balimo, and Kondobol, and will proceed to Morehead station tomorrow. The Kiunga relay station was previously established using the IP Link.

According to Western Provincial Administration ICT officer Michael Wangihomie, the Kiunga project is fully funded and installed by the Fly River Provincial Government and implemented by the Western provincial administration through the ICT division.

"It is currently carrying 90.7 National Radio direct from Port Moresby," Wangihomie said.

The restoration of the four remaining relay stations is funded by the Sustainable Development Program. The provincial government has also provided logistics support including IP Links for the Daru restoration.

Mr Wanghiomie said with the Daru studio now restored, the IP Link from Daru will be reactivated to transmit Radio Western to Kiunga.

"Nbc Engineers will also configure the Kiunga transmitter to broadcast Provincial Radio on 95.5.Once completed, Kiunga listeners will have access to Tribe FM 92.3, 90.7 National Radio, and 95.5 Provincial Radio," said Wangihomie.

NBC Western Management acknowledges the support from the Fly River Provincial Government through the Western Provincial Administration ICT Division, and the Sustainable Development Program in restoring national radio and local broadcasting services across Western Province.

The temporary studio will ensure continuous local content for Western Province listeners while work on the permanent facilities is completed.

item.title: FPDA delivers vital irrigation systems to help Gembogl farmers tackle El Niño
item.description: When El Niño dries up the soil across PNG, most farmers pray for rain. In the rugged mountains of Simbu, they are not waiting for the clouds, they are building their own. David Kaupa, the coordinator of FPDA in Simbu said this during the official opening of a water irrigation system installation in Kegesuglo, Kundiawa Gembogl District of Simbu this week.
item.content:encoded:
When El Niño dries up the soil across PNG, most farmers pray for rain. In the rugged mountains of Simbu, they are not waiting for the clouds, they are building their own.

David Kaupa, the coordinator of FPDA in Simbu said this during the official opening of a water irrigation system installation in Kegesuglo, Kundiawa Gembogl District of Simbu this week.

"With Simbu Province being PNG's leading producer of potato seeds, now a fresh push for self-reliance is keeping those crops alive despite severe drought. It's designed to counter the aggressive toll of the ongoing El Niño season and safeguard the country's seed supply", Mr. Kaupa said.

He also said the installation of this water system directly complements seed production so farmers can maintain supply despite the dry spell.

Lead farmer John Banda said for high-altitude communities, farming isn't just a livelihood—it's the local economy.

He said the initiative is already creating a chain reaction among neighbors.

He said most of the village relies on farming for income.

With this installation, they are able to assist surrounding farmers by extending water pipes directly to their plots.

According to FPDA is that; what makes this project unique is its funding-FPDA built this system using its internal resources, receiving zero government financial backing.

David Minemba, the research development project manager of FPDA said they are generating key data and now have enough evidence to prove to the government what works when shaping future agricultural policies for PNG.

"Beyond Simbu, FPDA is installing similar systems across Western Highlands, Jiwaka, Eastern Highlands, Morobe, and Central Provinces," he said.

He said the goal is twofold: survive the present drought and collect real-time agricultural data to shield PNG from future climate shocks.

He said FPDA hopes this data-driven model will encourage national leaders to invest heavily in climate-resilient farming before the next El Niño strikes. Its important to note agricultural data to shield PNG from future climate shocks.

item.title: Western Highlands praised for orderly PM’s Highway welcome
item.description: Western Highlands has been praised for the way it received Prime Minister James Marape and his delegation during their historic drive along the new Pangu Highway. Tambul-Nebilyer MP and Minister Assisting the Prime Minister, Win Daki, who travelled with the Prime Minister’s entourage, said the people of Western Highlands showed respect and discipline as the convoy entered the province from Jiwaka.
item.content:encoded:
Western Highlands has been praised for the way it received Prime Minister James Marape and his delegation during their historic drive along the new Pangu Highway.

Tambul-Nebilyer MP and Minister Assisting the Prime Minister, Win Daki, who travelled with the Prime Minister’s entourage, said the people of Western Highlands showed respect and discipline as the convoy entered the province from Jiwaka.

He said people gathered along the highway to witness the historic journey, but kept a safe distance and did not obstruct the convoy.

“When we entered Western Highlands, we could see people standing along the road to welcome the Prime Minister. But they respected the convoy and gave us space to move freely. There was no problem.”

The same order was maintained as the convoy moved into Mt Hagen City.

Daki said there were no vehicles deliberately blocking the road, with motorists and pedestrians instead standing aside to allow the delegation to pass.

He said he was proud of the people of Western Highlands for the way they conducted themselves.

The peaceful reception was also supported by a strong police presence.

Western Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent John Sagom said police officers were positioned along key points of the route, from the city towards Waghi and Komun bridges, to manage traffic and maintain public safety.

“Our main concern was to make sure the people were safe, the traffic was controlled and the convoy could move without any problems. Our officers were deployed along the route and we worked together to ensure everything remained peaceful.”

Governor Wai Rapa, Provincial Administrator Joseph Mangbil and PPC Sagom were also seen along the route, helping to coordinate the reception as the convoy travelled from Simbu towards Tuman Bridge.

The Governor later thanked Prime Minister Marape for the new highway, saying it would have a direct impact on the people of Western Highlands, particularly those involved in small businesses and agriculture.

“Our people are hardworking people. They toil the land, they produce food and many are involved in SMEs. This highway will make a big difference because it will give our people better access to markets and opportunities," Rapa stressed.

The orderly reception continued at Queen’s Park in Mt Hagen, where hundreds gathered to welcome Prime Minister Marape and his delegation at about five o’clock yesterday afternoon.

The programme continued into the evening before concluding at around eight o’clock in the night.

Police and security personnel remained on the ground as the travelling delegation retired for the night.

For Western Highlands, the reception was not only about welcoming the Prime Minister.

It was also a demonstration of how communities, provincial leaders and police can work together to host a major national event peacefully and safely.

item.title: Hela begins bore water drilling as El Niño response
item.description: The Hela provincial government today commenced its bore water drilling program at Tari Hospital, with Governor Philip Undialu witnessing the first drill bit being punched into the ground. Undialu described the first drilling as a significant moment for Hela, saying the current El Niño and prolonged dry spell had highlighted the urgent need for sustainable water security across the province.
item.content:encoded:
The Hela provincial government today commenced its bore water drilling program at Tari Hospital, with Governor Philip Undialu witnessing the first drill bit being punched into the ground.

Undialu described the first drilling as a significant moment for Hela, saying the current El Niño and prolonged dry spell had highlighted the urgent need for sustainable water security across the province.

“Today is a historic day for Hela. We are responding to the immediate water crisis caused by El Niño, but we are also looking beyond this crisis and investing in sustainable water sources for our people,” he said.

The governor said drilling also carried cultural and historical significance because of a long-held Hela oral tradition about an underground river known as Kukupia.

“Our people have spoken for generations about Kukupia, a river believed in our traditional stories to flow beneath the soil."

Undialu announced that the Hela provincial government is preparing a larger program involving approximately 10 major deep bore water sites, with proposed drilling depths of between 200 and 500 metres.

These deeper wells will prioritise main centres and critical institutions such as hospitals, schools and other public facilities.

He said the program will also include more than 200 shallower bore-water sites, generally targeting depths of approximately 40–50 metres, to extend reliable water access to villages and council wards across the province.

“The deep drilling will target our major centres and institutions, while the shallower drilling will take water security directly to our villages and wards. Our objective is to make sure that every community has access to a reliable source of water,” governor Undialu said.

He said the current dry spell had exposed the vulnerability of communities that depend heavily on rivers, streams and other seasonal water sources.

“El Niño has taught us a very important lesson. We cannot wait for the next drought before we think about water. We must use this crisis to build permanent solutions,” he said.

“This is not only about El Niño relief. It is about WASH, public health, human dignity and building a more resilient Hela for our children and grandchildren.”

Undialu said his administration would continue working with relevant national agencies, development partners and technical experts to ensure the bore-water program was properly planned, drilled and developed.

“Today we drill for water. Tomorrow we build water security. The first drill at Tari Hospital is only the beginning,” he said.

item.title: ​Alcohol-related hospital admissions drops following liquor ban in Hela
item.description: ​Alcohol-related violence in Hela Province has seen a dramatic decrease, leading to a major drop in emergency admissions at Tari Hospital, according to an official. Hela Provincial Health Authority [PHA] chief executive officer Dr. James Kintwa confirmed that admissions resulting from alcohol-fueled violence have fallen by 60 to 70 percent.
item.content:encoded:
​Alcohol-related violence in Hela Province has seen a dramatic decrease, leading to a major drop in emergency admissions at Tari Hospital, according to an official.

Hela Provincial Health Authority [PHA] chief executive officer Dr. James Kintwa confirmed that admissions resulting from alcohol-fueled violence have fallen by 60 to 70 percent.

Hel governor Philip Undialu said alcohol remains the leading driver of violence across the province. He reaffirmed that the Hela Provincial Liquor Licensing Board will maintain a close partnership with the police and PNGDF personnel to strictly enforce the ongoing liquor ban and curb smuggling operations.

​The Undialu revealed that a local school teacher is currently detained at the Tari Police Station cell block for allegedly attempting to smuggle alcohol into the province.

"Despite an active security checkpoint established at Magarima Station, the educator allegedly attempted to bypass the restriction in pursuit of quick financial gain," he said.

​Governor Undialu said public servants are expected to serve as role models within their communities and warned that anyone caught participating in illegal activities would face severe penalties and administrative discipline.

​"The ban was enacted in response to persistent calls from local churches, women's groups, and community leaders," he said.

"Special tribute to the late Janet Korima, the first woman to represent women’s interests in the Hela Provincial Assembly since 2013, who was a dedicated advocate for both the alcohol ban and the surrender of illegal firearms."

Undialu urged mothers, ward councilors, and community leaders to actively report anyone involved in the illegal sale or distribution of liquor to the police.

item.title: West Sepik businesses eye opportunities at Indonesia’s trade expo
item.description: Businesses in West Sepik are being encouraged to look beyond the province’s immediate markets and explore opportunities in Indonesia, with several local business representatives expressing interest in attending the 41st Trade Expo Indonesia later this year. The opportunity was highlighted during a meeting hosted by the Indonesian Consulate in Vanimo on September 2, bringing together representative
item.content:encoded:
Businesses in West Sepik are being encouraged to look beyond the province’s immediate markets and explore opportunities in Indonesia, with several local business representatives expressing interest in attending the 41st Trade Expo Indonesia later this year.

The opportunity was highlighted during a meeting hosted by the Indonesian Consulate in Vanimo on September 2, bringing together representatives of the West Sepik Provincial Government, the West Sepik Chamber of Commerce and businesses from Vanimo and surrounding areas.

The meeting provided local stakeholders with information on the Trade Expo Indonesia 2026, including the business opportunities available, participation requirements and arrangements for travel to Indonesia.

The five-day trade expo will be held from October 14 to 18 at the Indonesia Convention Exhibition in BSD City, Tangerang Regency, Banten Province.

For West Sepik, the expo presents an opportunity to strengthen the province's growing commercial relationship with Indonesia, particularly given Vanimo's strategic position along the PNG-Indonesia border.

The Indonesian Consul in Vanimo, Tangkuman Alexander told participants that the expo will bring together Indonesian producers and international buyers across a wide range of sectors, including agriculture and food, manufacturing, industrial products, fashion, handicrafts and furniture.

A key feature will be business-matching sessions, allowing overseas participants to meet directly with Indonesian companies and explore potential trade and investment partnerships.

For local businesses, this could provide a pathway to identify new markets, suppliers, products and technologies that could be relevant to West Sepik and other parts of Papua New Guinea.

The expo attracted more than 34,000 visitors and over 1,600 exhibitors in 2025, with organisers expecting an even larger turnout this year.

The scale of the event means West Sepik businesses attending will have the opportunity to see first-hand the range of products and enterprises operating in one of the region's major economies.

For small and medium-sized businesses in Vanimo, participation could also be a chance to learn how Indonesian enterprises process, package and market agricultural products and locally manufactured goods. This is particularly relevant for PNG businesses seeking to move beyond selling raw products and develop value-added products that can compete in wider markets.

The meeting also highlighted the possibility for participants to extend their trip after the expo to visit factories and home industries connected to their particular business interests.

Such visits could provide practical exposure to production methods and business models that could potentially be adapted to the PNG market.

The Indonesian Consulate also briefed participants on travel and visa arrangements.

PNG participants from West Sepik can use Indonesia's Visa on Arrival facility at the Skouw border post, while holders of official passports are exempt from visa requirements under the Indonesia-PNG visa-exemption arrangement, subject to the required passport validity.

Several business representatives who attended the Vanimo meeting have already indicated interest in participating in the expo.

The West Sepik Chamber of Commerce is expected to coordinate confirmation and follow-up arrangements with the Indonesian Consulate.

For West Sepik, the significance of the expo extends beyond individual businesses.

Greater participation could help build stronger commercial links between Vanimo and neighbouring Indonesian markets, opening possibilities for increased trade, investment, business knowledge and private-sector partnerships.

It could also position West Sepik businesses to contribute more actively to PNG's broader trade ambitions by connecting local enterprises with international buyers and business networks.

With Indonesia continuing to serve as PNG's immediate western neighbour and an important regional market, opportunities such as TEI 2026 could give businesses in Vanimo a platform to turn geographical proximity into practical economic partnerships.

item.title: K29.7 million secured to seal Kikiri road in Popondetta
item.description: Popondetta District has secured K29.7 million through the Kina for Kina and Public Investment Program to upgrade and seal Kikiri road in Northern Province. The announcement was made on Wednesday by local PM Richard Masere.
item.content:encoded:
Popondetta District has secured K29.7 million through the Kina for Kina and Public Investment Program to upgrade and seal Kikiri road in Northern Province.

The announcement was made on Wednesday by local PM Richard Masere.

Masere said the Kikiri road project will be rolled out in three phases over the next three years.

The first phase payment of K5 million has already been released. He said the K5 million will be used to seal one kilometre of the road.

The Kikiri road project has been awarded to Savana Construction Limited.

Speaking at the announcement, Savana Construction Managing Director Thomas Constan Tinou thanked Minister Masere and the Popondetta District DDA for awarding the project to his company.

Tinou said they will ensure the first phase is completed and they move on to the second and final stage of the project.
